messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Bengali, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Bengali line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
সেই ব্যক্তি তাকে প্রতিটি শহরে শিকার করবে, যতক্ষণ না সে তাকে নরকে ফিরে পাঠাবে, সেখানে যেখানে ঈর্ষা প্রথমে তাকে পাঠিয়েছিল।

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (Bengali) | Back‑Translation (English) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------|--------| | Questi | the male agent who performs the hunting | সেই ব্যক্তি | “that person / he” | OK | | la | patient of the hunt (her) | তাকে | “her” | OK | | caccerà | future action of pursuing (hunt) | শিকার করবে | “will hunt” | OK | | per | preposition marking traversal across locations | — (implicit in “শহরে”) | “through / in” | UNNECESSARY | | ogne | quantifier over towns (every) | প্রতিটি | “every” | OK | | villa | individual location being traversed (town) | শহরে | “in town” | OK | | fin | introduces temporal limit (till) | যতক্ষণ | “until / as long as” | OK | | che | subordinator introducing the endpoint clause (that) | না | “that … not” (part of “যতক্ষণ না”) | OK | | l’avrà | auxiliary forming future‑perfect (shall have) | — (absorbed in verb) | “shall have” | UNNECESSARY | | rimessa | action of returning her to a place (set back) | ফিরে পাঠাবে | “will send back” | OK | | ne | preposition “in” (locative) | — (implicit in “নরকে”) | “in” | UNNECESSARY | | lo | definite article “the” | — (implicit) | “the” | UNNECESSARY | | ’nferno | destination “hell” | নরকে | “to hell” | OK | | là | locative adverb “there” | সেখানে | “there” | OK | | onde | relative adverb “whence” (introduces causal clause) | যেখানে | “where / whence” | OK | | ’nvidia | personified force “envy” | ঈর্ষা | “envy” | OK | | prima | temporal qualifier “first” | প্রথমে | “first” | OK | | dipartilla | future action of dispatching her (send forth) | পাঠিয়েছিল | “sent her” (past narrative) | OK |
---
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: `per`, `ne`, `lo`, `l’avrà` – these grammatical particles are not overtly expressed in Bengali; their meaning is conveyed by case marking or verb morphology. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** issues were detected. The Bengali rendering respects number, gender (neutral in Bengali), and verb‑aspect conventions.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Bengali script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Bengali text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
